nodes.name: ZIF-8 Synthesis
nodes.procedure: 1.36 g Zn(NO3)2·6H2O and 1.5 g 2-Melm were dissolved in 25 mL methanol solution, respectively. Then the two solutions were mixed and stirred for 30 min. ZIF-8 was obtained by centrifugation and then dried in the oven at 60°C for 4 h. [24].
nodes.source_text: 1.36 g Zn(NO3)2·6H2O and 1.5 g 2-Melm were dissolved in 25 mL methanol solution, respectively. Then the two solutions were mixed and stirred for 30 min. ZIF-8 was obtained by centrifugation and then dried in the oven at 60°C for 4 h. [24].

nodes.name: BI@ZIF-8 One-pot Synthesis
nodes.procedure: 1.36 g Zn(NO3)2·6H2O and 1.5 g 2-Melm were dissolved in 25 mL methanol solution, respectively. Then the 2 mg/mL methanolic solution of BI was added to the solution of 2-Melm with stirring for 10 min. Then the solution of Zn(NO3)2·6H2O was added to the mixed solution with stirring for 30 min. ZB was obtained by centrifugation and drying.
nodes.source_text: BI@ZIF-8 (ZB) was synthesized by the one-pot method. 1.36 g Zn(NO3)2·6H2O and 1.5 g 2-Melm were dissolved in 25 mL methanol solution, respectively. Then the 2 mg/mL methanolic solution of BI was added to the solution of 2-Melm with stirring for 10 min.

nodes.name: ZBT Hydrophilic Modification
nodes.procedure: The synthesis method of ZBT was shown in Fig. 1. 0.1 g ZB were dissolved in the water to get the suspension of ZB. During the process, TA (12 mol/L solution, pH = 8) was added into the suspension of ZB. After settling for 2 h, ZBT were obtained by centrifugation and drying.

nodes.source_text: The synthesis method of ZBT was shown in Fig. 1. 0.1 g ZB were dissolved in the water to get the suspension of ZB. During the process, TA (12 mol/L solution, pH = 8) was added into the suspension of ZB. After settling for 2 h, ZBT were obtained by centrifugation and drying.

nodes.name: ZBT/EP Coating Preparation
nodes.procedure: ZBT was dissolved into 10 g epoxy resin and ultrasonic dispersion for 1 h. Then 10 g curing agent was added to the mixed liquor with ultrasonic dispersion for 1 h to obtain the ZBT/EP composite coatings. The ZBT/EP composite coatings were applied to the prepared Q235 carbon steel (polished by 100#, 400# and 800# grade sandpapers and washed by acetone) and dried for 7 d at room temperature (25°C). The loading ratio of the prepared nanoparticles in the coatings was 0.5 wt%.

nodes.description: Pull-off adhesion strength test (original and after 173 days immersion)
nodes.source_text: The original adhesion strengths of the coatings were 8.85MPa, 10.44MPa, 10.49MPa and 10.83MPa, respectively. The wet adhesion strength at the end of the immersion experiment (173 d) of the coatings decreased to 3.11MPa, 7.48MPa, 7.7MPa and 7.89MPa, respectively. The wet adhesion loss of EP and ZBT/EP coatings was 63.6% and 27.1%, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Characteristic peaks of ZIF-8 at 1145 cm⁻¹ (C=N), 995 cm⁻¹ (C-N), 755 cm⁻¹ (Zn-O), 422 cm⁻¹ (Zn-N); ZB shows additional 1268 cm⁻¹ (C-H from BI); ZBT shows 3400 cm⁻¹ (-OH) and 1695 cm⁻¹ (C=O from TA).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The characteristic peaks observed at 1145 cm⁻¹, 995 cm⁻¹, 755 cm⁻¹ and 422 cm⁻¹ in ZIF-8 were ascribed to C=N, C-N in the imidazole ring, the Zn-O bond, and the tensile vibration of the Zn-N bond, respectively. ... Two new characteristic peaks in ZBT appeared at 3400 cm⁻¹ and 1695 cm⁻¹ were ascribed to -OH and C=O in TA, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: ZIF-8, ZB, and ZBT show main diffraction peaks at 2θ = 7.3° (011), 12.9° (112), 18.2° (222) with no change in crystalline structure after BI loading and TA modification; sharp peaks indicate high crystallinity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XRD patterns of ZIF-8, ZB and ZBT were displayed in Fig. 2(b). The main diffraction peaks of ZIF-8 at 2θ = 7.3°, 12.9°, and 18.2° corresponded to the (011), (112), and (222) planes of ZIF-8 crystal, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: ZIF-8 shows 20 wt% loss at 130-650°C and total 36 wt% at 800°C. ZB shows 37 wt% loss at 130-650°C (BI decomposition) and total 49 wt% at 800°C. ZBT shows 5 wt% loss at 25-130°C (water/solvents), 44 wt% at 130-650°C (BI/TA), 12 wt% at 650-800°C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The TGA curves and DTG curves of ZIF-8, ZB, ZBT TA and BI were shown in Fig. 2(c) and (d), respectively. ... From the TGA and DTG results, the thermal decomposition rates of ZIF-8, ZB, and ZBT were about the same after 650°C, and it was considered that BI and TA in ZBT had been completely decomposed at 650°C, the weight fraction of BI and TA was 17 wt% and 12 wt%, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: ZIF-8 shows rhombic dodecahedral crystals (80-110 nm). ZB shows spherical morphology with rough surface (500-800 nm). ZBT shows rougher surface (1200-1600 nm).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The surface morphology and particle size distribution were displayed in Fig. 3. As shown in Fig. 3(a₁,a₂), ZIF-8 was a rhombic dodecahedral crystal, and the size mainly distributed in 80 nm∼110 nm.

properties.description: Dark background with bright scattered particles/dots

nodes.characterization_summary: Contact angles: ZIF-8 = 83.5° (hydrophobic), ZB = 75° (increased roughness), ZBT = 64° (hydrophilic modification by TA).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 4 displayed the contact angles of ZIF-8, ZB and ZBT. The contact angle of ZIF-8 was 83.5° for its hydrophobicity, as shown in Fig. 4(a).

nodes.characterization_summary: ZBT shows higher O content than ZB (TA modification). Zn 2p peaks negatively shifted in ZBT (BI-Zn coordination). C 1s: 284.78 eV (C-C/C=C), 285.85 eV (C-N), 287.40 eV (C=O from TA). N 1s: 398.88 eV (C-N), 399.53 eV (C=N), 400.1 eV (Zn-N).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XPS spectra of ZIF-8, ZB and ZBT were displayed in Fig. 5. From Fig. 5(a), the O ratios in ZBT were higher than those in ZB which indicated the successful modification of TA.

nodes.characterization_summary: BI release from ZBT: at pH 5 and 10, 72.4% and 68.4% released in first 3h; slower release at pH 7 prevents leakage during coating cure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The release curves of BI from ZBT at different pH values were shown in Fig. 6(b). During the first 3 h, BI was released faster at pH = 5 and pH = 10, and the release amount reached 72.4% and 68.4%, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Cross-section SEM shows ZBT/EP coatings have highest compactness with uniform Zn distribution confirmed by EDS mapping.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 7 displayed the cross-section morphology of the coatings and the EDS images of the main elements in the ZBT/EP coatings. The EP coatings had a small micropores and the ZBT/EP coatings was the most compactness.
